segments.title: Chương 157: Lý Quân và Trần Quý Lương là anh em
segments.content:
Chapter 160 | 0157 Li Jun: Chen Guiliang and I are bros.

Bian Guanyue's father, Bian Jinsong, also had a very rich life experience.

After resigning from his teaching job back in the day, Bian Jinsong had worked in many industries.

What prompted him to start a business was a news report about a young man named Yang Zuwei, who had started selling mosquito nets from a street stall in 1980 and earned 1 million yuan in six years. He became the first millionaire in all of Sichuan!

Spurred on, Bian Jinsong also went to sell mosquito nets.

Then he discovered that Qingnian Road was full of people selling mosquito nets. And most of the stall owners had gotten the bright idea to jump into business only after reading that same report.

And the one wholesaling the nylon mosquito nets to them was none other than that millionaire, Yang Zuwei…

Bian Jinsong's first entrepreneurial attempt thus ended in failure. There were too many competitors, and he couldn't sell them at all. In the end, he could only give the remaining mosquito nets to relatives and friends for free.

Next, he borrowed over a thousand yuan from his parents, sister, and friends, and started riding his bicycle to collect used goods to sell at the Chenghuangmiao Market. After two years of hard work and toil, once he had paid off his debts, he had only saved up a little over 3,000 yuan.

For the next two years, he set up a stall to sell electronic products, like calculators and digital watches. He earned a lot when he first entered the trade, but competition became fierce in the second year, and the streets were full of people selling the same things.

It was also at this time that he met that beautiful widow, which led to a messy divorce from his first wife.

Bian Jinsong chose to leave the marriage with nothing. He gave the 36,000-plus yuan he had saved over the years entirely to Bian Guanyue's biological mother, leaving himself with only some unsold electronic products.

At that time, an unofficial stock market appeared around the Chenghuangmiao area of Chengdu—the Shanghai Stock Exchange had not even been established yet.

After his divorce, Bian Jinsong didn't immediately marry his second wife. But he borrowed 3,000 yuan from that woman, bought 15 shares of stock in Chenghuangmiao, and in less than a week, 3,000 yuan turned into 8,000 yuan!

Bian Jinsong was quite regretful; if he had sold just two days later, it would have become 10,000 yuan straight away.

He threw all 8,000 yuan back in, continuing to buy stocks. Five months later, it had turned into 130,000 yuan!

These stocks were all illegally issued by private entities, all traded face-to-face in private transactions.

Moreover, they only went up, never down.

The more Bian Jinsong played the stock market, the more nervous he became. When his net worth swelled to 200,000, he pulled out and went to open a restaurant. Due to poor management, he lost 40,000 yuan in half a year and had to close down and transfer the storefront.

After two years of this, changing industries several times, his 200,000 yuan had dwindled to just 50,000.

Hearing about a real estate speculation craze on Hainan Island, Bian Jinsong and his second wife each invested 50,000 yuan and went to Hainan to speculate on land. In just over a year, the 100,000 yuan they had brought with them snowballed into more than 4 million.

Then it almost led to a divorce. Bian Jinsong felt they should quit while they were ahead, but his second wife believed prices would continue to rise.

The couple argued endlessly and could only split the money and part ways.

Bian Jinsong took 2 million yuan back to his hometown, while his wife took the other 2 million-plus to continue speculating on land. They agreed to file for divorce once she returned.

Three months later, his second wife lost everything!

But the divorce never happened. The woman was pregnant…

In 1994, the Funan River renovation project was launched. More than 60,000 households needed to be relocated, and several real estate companies sprang up in response.

Through his second wife's family connections, Bian Jinsong also founded a real estate company. But he only got some scraps, and the land he acquired was only enough to build a single residential community.

Today, Bian Jinsong's main business is in the hotel industry, with a side of real estate.

Perhaps it was his past entrepreneurial experiences that made him extremely cautious in business now. During the era of the real estate boom, Bian Jinsong surprisingly did not expand aggressively.

His approach was to play it safe and steady.

"President Bian, here are today's newspapers, and these are the documents that need your signature…"

His female secretary was very beautiful, and full of charm.

This was a test Bian Jinsong was putting his wife through. He had transferred his previous male secretary to a hotel as a department manager. He had specifically switched to a beautiful female secretary to see when his wife would come to the company to cause a scene.

His father-in-law had been dead for two years, and Bian Jinsong no longer wanted to be controlled by his wife.

He had had enough!

Changing secretaries was just the first step. Next, he would replace several mid-to-high-level executives in the company—all of whom were his wife's relatives and friends.

If his wife reacted too strongly, he wouldn't mind sending one or two of them to prison.

He had long since collected enough evidence.

After signing the documents, Bian Jinsong sat in his office and read the newspaper.

The secretary had already organized the papers, with important news highlighted for Bian Jinsong's quick reading.

The *People's Daily*, *Guangming Daily*, *Southern Metropolis Daily*, *West China Metropolis Daily*… and several mainstream financial newspapers.

In the last two years, Chengdu's real estate market had developed rapidly.

The average price in 2003 was only 1,911 yuan, but it doubled directly to 3,713 yuan in 2004.

This year, the "Eight National Measures" were introduced as the central government tried to cool down the real estate market. Housing prices for new developments in Shanghai had plummeted by 30 or 40 percent.

But prices in Chengdu were still rising, just not as fiercely as last year. The current average price had already increased to 3,900 yuan.

Could his judgment have been wrong? Had he been too cautious with his investments?

Bian Jinsong felt like he could no longer keep up with the times. He always waited until he had relatively ample funds before taking out loans to acquire land and build new properties. He had wasted so many opportunities!

His wife, on the other hand, was much more aggressive. Due to their differing business philosophies, the couple had argued countless times over the past two years.

"Huh?"

Although the reporters from the *West China Metropolis Daily* hadn't been invited to Beijing this time, their sister publication, the *National Business Daily*, had brought back plenty of interview material.

"19-Year-Old Sichuan Kid Becomes a Hundred-Millionaire!"

A full-page report.

"Over the past year, this newspaper has followed the story of Chen Guiliang, who was specially admitted to Peking University with a reduced score. From an ordinary third-year high school student, he entered Peking University thanks to the New Concept Writing Competition…"

"Just last weekend, ByteDance, the company founded by Chen Guiliang, received a total of 5 million USD in investment from two venture capital firms, IDG and DFJ… The company's post-money valuation is 30 million USD, which is 248 million RMB. Chen Guiliang personally holds 64.4% of the shares, making his net worth approximately 160 million RMB…"

"And all of this happened the day before his 19th birthday. Chen Guiliang said this was the best birthday present he could give himself…"

"From a left-behind child in rural southern Sichuan to the boss of a tech company worth over a hundred million, Chen Guiliang completed this magnificent transformation in just one year…"

Bian Jinsong was dumbfounded, holding the newspaper and speechless for a long time.

Had he really fallen behind the times?

He had struggled for so many years and had built a large company. But excluding the shares held by his wife, brother-in-law, and sister's husband, his own shares were only worth a little over one hundred million after depreciation, the vast majority of which were fixed assets.

How had his daughter's boyfriend surpassed him in just one year?

He had Chen Guiliang's phone number.

After some thought, he dialed it.

"Hello, Uncle Bian, I'm in class…" The voice on the other end was very low.

In class?

The expression on Bian Jinsong's face became even more incredulous. He felt like he had wasted half his life.

"Then I won't disturb your class. I'll call you at noon," Bian Jinsong said.

They said their goodbyes and hung up.

Bian Jinsong then called his wife. "Big Sis (nickname), have you seen the *West China Metropolis Daily*? No, nothing… Remember that young man we met at the airport when we took Guanguan to school? Haha, that kid started a company, and his net worth is higher than mine now… I'm not lying, find a newspaper and see for yourself…"

After finishing the call with his wife, Bian Jinsong grew a little worried about his daughter.

He knew all too well that once a man becomes successful, there's never a shortage of beautiful women around him. That kid wouldn't dump his daughter, would he?

He picked up the phone and put it down again, afraid of disturbing his daughter's studies.

It wasn't until noon that Bian Jinsong finally called his daughter. "Guanguan, are you still dating Chen Guiliang?"

"Yeah," Bian Guanyue admitted openly.

"Has he… has he…" Bian Jinsong didn't know how to put it.

Bian Guanyue asked, "Has he what?"

"Nothing," Bian Jinsong said. "You have a bad temper sometimes. Don't throw little tantrums at your boyfriend, especially when he's busy with important things. If he makes some kind of mistake, don't just start a fight right away. You should be more strategic… If it really doesn't work out, then just break up."

Bian Guanyue was completely baffled. "What on earth are you trying to say?"

"Dad's been through this… um, you know about your uncle, right?" Bian Jinsong began to give an example.

Bian Guanyue said angrily, "Chen Guiliang is nothing like my uncle!"

Bian Jinsong said, "I'm not saying he's definitely like your uncle. I'm saying that when a man's career becomes successful, he's bound to face all sorts of temptations. You need to be mentally prepared and stay calm when things happen. Don't be like you are at home, losing your temper with me at the drop of a hat. That only makes conflicts worse. I know telling you this now isn't very useful, but I'm just giving you a heads-up. If he goes too far, you should break up with him early. The longer you drag it out, the more painful it will be."

"I'm hanging up. Goodbye." Sitting in the cafeteria, Bian Guanyue held her phone, feeling a little dazed.

Her dad's words had made her feel a pang of insecurity.

The evening of the investment signing ceremony.

Sichuan University campus.

"Holy crap!"

A guy from the next dorm who had a computer yelled out and rushed into Xu Haibo's room. "Bobo, get over here and look at this."

"What's wrong?" Xu Haibo had just gotten back from his tutoring job.

The guy said, "Don't you always brag about how Chen Guiliang was your high school roommate? Damn, he's a hundred-millionaire now!"

Xu Haibo and his roommates curiously ran to the next dorm and crowded around the computer to take a closer look.

Two hours ago, an article and photos from the investment ceremony had been posted on the campus network's homepage.

Xu Haibo was completely stunned. "A… a net worth of over one hundred million?"

"Whoa, his 19th birthday is tomorrow. He's four months younger than me," said the guy in the bunk above Xu Haibo. "I only get 300 yuan a month for living expenses, and he's already a hundred-millionaire."

"Bobo, if I were you, I'd go work at Chen Guiliang's company after graduation. You'd definitely get special treatment!"

"So awesome, he's basically my idol!"

"Bobo, where are you going?"

"The internet cafe!"

Xu Haibo sprinted to an internet cafe off-campus, turned on a computer, and logged into QQ.

Just as expected, the high school class group chat was buzzing with activity.
